moat_against: ROIC collapsed after the GW acquisition: roic_proxy 1.4%/-0.7%/5.8%/7.3%/-4.1% for 2021-25 vs 10-13% in 2016-19
Xywav concentration (~39% of Q2 2026 revenue) faces generic high-sodium oxybate payer pressure from H2 2026 and once-nightly Lumryz
Orexin agonists in development (Takeda, Axsome) threaten the narcolepsy franchise longer term
Growth is bought: recurring acquisition IPR&D ($948M in 2025, Chimerix; $820M Actio closed Sep 2026) sits outside owner's earnings
moat_for: Oxybate REMS controlled-distribution platform creates switching friction for Xywav/Xyrem
Epidiolex patent protection into the late 2030s (ANDA litigations resolved)
High product gross margins (~88% GAAP per company guidance) on orphan/rare-disease pricing
Diversifying oncology launches: Ziihera (HER2+ GEA, peak sales est. raised to $3-5B) and Modeyso
moat_justification: Patent-protected niche franchises with real friction — oxybate REMS controlled distribution, Epidiolex patents into the late 2030s, ~88% GAAP gross margin — but returns on the acquisition-inflated capital base have been poor: roic_proxy 10-13% in 2016-19 fell to 1.4% (2021), -0.7% (2022), 5.8% (2023), 7.3% (2024), -4.1% (2025, IPR&D-depressed). The largest franchise (Xywav) faces generic high-sodium oxybate payer pressure, once-nightly Lumryz, and orexin agonists in development. Moderate/narrow moat, not wide.
name: Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc
one_liner: Cash-generative specialty pharma, moat 5/10 — clears 15% only just and only on the TTM base (weighted IRR 15.4%, IV@15 $218 vs $210 price); on the 3-yr median base it does not clear (14.2%, Tier C), so size it to the bear end, not as a full B.
